rationale: Replacing plain FM with a Field-aware FM (separate embedding per interacting field pair, k=6) plus a within-user-day position feature derived from time_ms will beat the FM baseline (valid 0.6016) by more than the 0.002 noise threshold, reaching ~0.604 valid primary, because FFM lets user_id's embedding toward videos differ from its embedding toward authors/position, and position captures feed order bias that varies within a user's impression list.

Continuous train-only item-side engagement features (smoothed long_view rate, impression count, mean duration-normalized watch proxy) computed strictly from the train split and added as extra numeric fields to the FFM will improve within-user ranking beyond FFM+position (valid 0.6045), because these vary within a user's impression list (item-side) and were never tested continuously before (prior 'static features' ablation only tried redundant categorical video IDs, not continuous rates). This is a genuinely new angle: encoding continuous train-only aggregates as bucketed categorical fields inside the existing FFM, not a GBDT (which failed due to axis-aligned splits on sparse user-item interactions, not due to the feature itself).
